page: Amazon Web Services r7g.large is an entry-tier instance within the memory-optimized EC2 portfolio, built on the AWS Nitro System. The instance operates on the arm64 architecture, powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors based on ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 cores running at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapped directly to 2 vCPUs. The processor cache hierarchy consists of 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, along with 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported through native AES instructions, while x86-specific vector and matrix extensions are absent.

System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for persistent block storage. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark data displays solid single-core metrics alongside expected multi-core limitations typical of a two-core virtual machine. Single-threaded tasks demonstrate mid-tier throughput, registered by a Geekbench single-core score of 1452.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 1532.49. In contrast, multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with Geekbench multi-core at 2589.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.0 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals average performance on large uncached read blocks at 53.89 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2390.88, while write bandwidth reaches 20.68 GB/sec.

The r7g.large instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy setups requiring a high RAM allocation per core without paying for unneeded CPU processing power. Workloads aligned with this footprint include small in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, relational caching tiers, mid-scale database replicas, and lightweight microservices with high memory demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.large is a memory-optimized arm64 instance powered by AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processors operating at 2.6 GHz. Hosted on the Nitro System, it delivers 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core and 16.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on Amazon EBS for persistent storage, and maintains a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect steady mid-tier single-threaded compute and memory read bandwidth, offset by low aggregate multi-core throughput due to its two-core ceiling. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides economical resource distribution for memory-bound applications that do not require dense compute capabilities. Typical operational fits include small Redis and Memcached caching instances, lightweight relational database workloads, microservices, and memory-intensive data ingestion tasks.
